rule: the committed tolerance must be >= the worst |fp16 - fp32| score gap over every reranked candidate of every golden query, with headroom; and selection must be STABLE -- the fp16 answer's ordered event ids identical to fp32-exact on every query. A lossy encoding that reorders the answer is not a smaller store, it is a different database.
note: S7, D-049. The first negotiated accuracy contract. fp32-exact remains the only DEFAULT; fp16 is opt-in, and a part written under it declares encoding_id=2, accuracy_contract_id=2 so a build that does not implement the contract refuses the part rather than guessing. Corpus- and generation-conditional.

real-v1.note: SHIPPED measurement. Real 768d normalized vectors have tiny per-component magnitudes, so the fp16 rounding gap is SMALLER than the hash corpus's (4.28e-5 vs 4.6e-4). Tolerance 2e-3 holds with 46.7x headroom, selection stable. NOT codebook-dependent — fp16 rounds the raw stored vectors, so this is independent of KMEANS_RESTARTS.

hash-v1.note: Retained paired series. Hash 64d vectors have larger per-component magnitudes, so the fp16 gap (~4.6e-4) is ~10x the real 768d gap. Tolerance 2e-3 bounds it with ~4.3x headroom.

delta.mechanism: The fp16 tolerance is a CONSERVATIVE contract bound, not tightened to any single corpus. The measured worst gap is geometry-dependent (real 768d 4.28e-5 vs hash 64d 4.6e-4) but the VALUE holds across both with large headroom, so it is classified geometry-STABLE — re-VERIFIED per corpus (it must still bound the gap), not re-derived. It is NOT downstream of KMEANS_RESTARTS: fp16 rounds the raw stored vectors, independent of the codebook.

_classification_note: geometry-STABLE: a conservative contract bound that held (46.7x headroom) across the hash and real corpora. Re-verify per corpus that it still bounds the measured gap; do NOT tighten to a single corpus (a different corpus may have a larger gap). tests/rederive_fp16.rs asserts tolerance>=max_gap and selection stability.
